new_statements.rule_in_words: Stokhof states that the position of the prominence peak (stress) is phonemically distinctive in Kabola and gives minimal pairs; stress is marked before the stressed syllable in every transcribed word (initial in e.g. /'mesa(y)/ 'table', /'tabaŋ/, /'dar/; final in /ta'rop/ 'bone', /fa'lad/ 'lungs', /pa'nen/, /na'fel/). No default position (penultimate or final) is stated, and the minimal pairs partly involve morphological structure (prefix+stem vs. compound/phrase: /na'fel/ 'my ear' vs. /'na fel/ 'to buy something'; /'bu hɛr/ noun phrase vs. /bu 'hɛr/ clause), so the contrast is at least partly grammatical rather than purely lexical.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed in Stokhof 1987. Stokhof 1975 (wordlist conventions, p. 3) notes that longer words may show two prominence peaks, one (') phonetically heavier than the other ("); no rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. Related remarks: unstressed /ɪ/~/y/ and /u/~/w/ are neutralised after a vowel before consonant or pause (sec. 3.1.7); the object noun /na/ 'thing(s)' usually forms one accentual unit with a following verb (sec. 6.1 (4)); /mi/ 'in' carries stress and is 'not a clitic' in the text (commentary note 68).
new_statements.domain_note: Word / accentual unit in elicited text from one speaker (Christoffel Foang, b. 1943 in Adang, resident in Jakarta since 1968); the minimal pairs span words and two-word accentual units (noun phrase vs. clause). Explicit (non-elliptic) subcode, i.e. careful citation-style speech, per sec. 3.1.11.
new_statements.identity_note: Stokhof 1987 (p. 631) treats 'Kabola' as one language with three regional variants: Adang/Pitumbang (villages Alor Kecil, Alor Besar, Ampera, Dulolong, Aimoli, Adang, Alila, Otuai), Kabola proper (Lawahing, Kabola) and Hamap. Glottolog now splits these as Adang [adn] adan1251, Kabola [klz] kabo1247 and Hamap [hmu] hama1240. Stokhof's text came from Christoffel Foang, born 1943 in Adang village (Pitumbang area), so the described variety may be closer to Glottolog's Adang (adan1251) than to Kabola proper; Glottolog and Klamer 2017 nonetheless file Stokhof 1987 under Kabola (kabo1247), and the statement is recorded here under that code with this caveat.

readall_conflicts: Stokhof 1987 (sec. 3.1.10, p. 633) claims the place of the prominence peak is distinctive, giving pairs such as /na'fel/ 'my ear' vs /'na fel/ 'to buy something', /'tabaŋ/ 'to add to one's questions' vs /ta'baŋ/ 'to ask us', /'bu hɛr/ 'a fallen areca nut' vs /bu 'hɛr/ 'an areca nut falls'. Haan 2001 (pp. 27-28), describing the same Adang variety, presents the equivalent pairs (tabáŋ / ta-bá:ŋ / tá ba:ŋ; bɛ́ hɛr vs bɛ́ hɛ́r; á fai vs á fái) and concludes that the differing stress positions 'distinguish different types of utterances (words, phrases, idioms serial verbs and clauses), but does not distinguish one word from another': word stress is fixed on the final syllable, with first-word stress in compounds/phrases/serial verbs. The two sources agree on the surface accent placements and disagree only on the analysis (lexically distinctive vs fixed: final syllable plus phrasal rule); Haan's examination of the actual morphology of each pair is the more explicit argument. Neither source is about Kabola proper by present-day classification.
